# Status and badges

> Settled 2026-09-09. Answers `analysis/ui/STATUS_AND_BADGES.md` — the archived look, the copies, the
> tokens and the archive verb; what that file still holds is where the code disagrees, plus the
> questions below.

## 1. One chip

`components/ui/StatusBadge` is the only status chip in the product. It was built during wave 4 of the
campaign, replacing five private copies of `statusBadge(status)` that had already drifted — the
leave-type one had no Draft, the calendar ones called the neutral state Inactive and the policy ones
called it Draft.

An entity maps its own enum onto the shared vocabulary and writes nothing else:

```tsx
const policyStatus = (status: TimeOffPolicyStatus): EntityStatus => {
  switch (status) {
    case TimeOffPolicyStatus.Active:   return "active";
    case TimeOffPolicyStatus.Archived: return "archived";
    default:                            return "draft";
  }
};

<StatusBadge status={policyStatus(policy.status)} />
```

**The mapping is the only thing a caller writes.** No colours, no labels, no `variant`.

A person's status has its own chip, `UserStatusBadge`, which replaced three byte-for-byte copies in the
People table and the two assigned-users views — and, since 2026-10-30, the person profile header. **Every
status chip is on the shared one**: the department and team panels and canvas nodes, the job catalog, the
office and legal-entity detail headers and the Assign roles dialog moved onto it that day. (`PersonChip`'s
grey *Archived* under a name is a subtitle, not a chip, and stays.)

## 2. Archived is grey

`Archived` is a **grey** chip. Not amber, not brown, not a plain outline — the product had all four
for the same concept, so an archived role looked brown, an archived leave type amber, and an archived
user grey.

Grey and not amber because **archived is not a warning**. It is a state somebody chose, reversible by
decision, and colouring it amber puts it in the same visual class as "something needs attention".

The row itself is **not** dimmed. Four modules added `opacity-60`, one added `border-dashed`, and the
rest added nothing; the chip says it, and dimming an entire row makes its text harder to read for a
reason that is already on screen. With the archived toggle now switching between two views
([`ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md`](ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md) § 5), an archived record is usually the *only* kind on
screen — dimming every row would be absurd.

**A canvas node is the one place a border stays.** The archived org-unit nodes lost their opacity and
kept `border-dashed`, because there the dash distinguishes a node's shape rather than fading its text.

## 3. Nine status tones, one tag palette, nothing else

Since 2026-11-04 the colours are the noddo design system's (SPEC §§ 4.5, 4.7; `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`).

**A status is one of nine tones** — approved, pending, in-progress, scheduled, declined, info, draft,
inactive, archived — drawn by `StatusBadge` as an icon and a word on the tone's soft background. An
entity maps its own enum onto them (`ProcessStatusBadge`, `RuleStatusBadge`, the review badges) and
writes no colour of its own. Status colours are **never themed**: Approved is Pine and an error is red
in every workspace, which is why a red or yellow company colour is allowed. Red appears only on a failed
field, a destructive label and a toast icon; banners and pages stay neutral.

**A category is not a status.** A user-chosen colour — a leave type, an option of a select attribute,
a lane, a notification tag — is one of the eight **tag colours** (gray, berry, plum, indigo, ocean,
teal, cocoa, bronze), stored by name and drawn by `TagChip` or the tag tokens. The chip per attribute
type in Field access and the National / Regional badge on holiday templates are tag chips too.

The old scales (`success-*`, `danger-*`, `warning-*`, `info-*`) and the brown chrome are gone: Tailwind
no longer knows them, and `test/designSystemGuard.test.ts` fails on them along with every raw palette
hue.

## 4. The archive vocabulary

**`Archive` ↔ `Unarchive`.** Everywhere, for every entity.

`Restore` and `Activate` were both used for leaving the archive — and on policies `Activate` *also*
meant draft → active, so one word covered two different transitions. `Restore` survives in exactly
one place and belongs there: the personal-documents **trash**, which is a trash with a retention
period, not an archive.

`Activate` / `Deactivate` remain, meaning what they say: whether an already-unarchived record is in
force. On a time off policy, unarchiving returns it to **Draft** and activating it is a second,
deliberate step — that separation is the point, not an inconvenience.

## What this does not settle

- The words for "not active yet": `Draft` (policies), `Not started` (people), `Inactive` (holiday
  calendars) — three words for adjacent ideas, still open.
- ~~`Not started` and `Archived` render identically on the profile header~~ — since 2026-11-04 a person
  before their start is `scheduled` (blue) and an archived one `archived` (gray).
- Whether the notification approval outcome (text colour, no chip) should become a chip.
